card.band: 8h. Many independent operators each give steady credit. A frontier agent speeds up the matmul and misses the others. Overlaps existing quantised-kernel cards (K1 risk).
card.cheat: Skipping computation is closed by randomised hidden shapes and tolerance checks.
card.grading: Hidden shape sweeps compare the outputs of each operator to the shipped baseline implementation within a per-dtype tolerance (exact for integer paths). Reward from the wall-clock median speedup across operator buckets. testOps is the visible self-check.
card.reference: Our own tuned kernels; the measured speedup S comes from the harness. Whether a later upstream version has a CPU speedup was not verified, so the card is a perf task rather than a verified release pair.
card.task: /app ships a history-less CPU-only snapshot of fastllm (no GPU backends) with the ./build/testOps operator tests. The agent speeds up the hot CPU operators (quantised linear, attention, RMSNorm, softmax, rotary) on 8 cores while keeping outputs within tolerance.
card.title: fastllm CPU operator kernel speedup under the testOps gate

source_notes: SWE-smith profile (cpp): its suite runs in a container; test command: ./build/testOps. The repo is used by a SWE-bench-family dataset.

spike_plan.kill_if: The build needs GPU or network; the CPU operators are unreachable from the CPU path; headroom is under 1.2x on every operator with noise above 20%.
spike_plan.pass_if: CPU-only build completes offline in under 20 minutes; optest runs deterministically; timing noise under 10%; a single change gives at least 1.5x on quantised linear with outputs matching; at least three of the five operator families are reachable on the CPU path.
steps: In a networked throwaway container, clone ztxz16/fastllm at 6caa8f7a and configure a CPU-only Release build (no CUDA/ROCm, no Python API); time the build and check for network fetches.
Build the optest target and run it three times; check runtime and whether the output is deterministic.
Locate the CPU entry points for linear, attention, RMSNorm, softmax and rotary (start in src/devices/cpu/cpudevice.cpp and linear.cpp) and record which exist.
Write a small timing script over three shapes per operator with median of seven runs at 8 threads; time single-thread against 8-thread to see existing parallelism.
Repeat the timing three times to estimate noise under gVisor-like conditions.
Try one quick change to the quantised linear loop (for example, threading the outer loop); check outputs against the baseline within tolerance and measure the speedup.

v1.summary: The card is real (Apache-2.0 fastllm, pinned commit 6caa8f7a with a CPU backend, multi-operator buckets and a continuous speedup reward) and no kill gate fails outright. It needs fixing before build: the named testOps target is not in the pinned CMake (optest and regressionOps are), the head claim is contradicted (master is 17 commits past the pin), the attention/RMSNorm/softmax/rotary CPU files are unconfirmed, and the reference kernels do not yet exist, so a 60-minute spike must confirm headroom and timing noise first.
